title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes build the inverse Cartier isomorphism and the Cartier operator for a morphism X→S in characteristic p, in a generalised setting. The relative Frobenius f = F_{X/S}: X → X^{(p/S)} is only assumed to have a local p-basis, and the target is twisted by Λ = Im(O_{X^{(p/S)}} → f_*O_X). The previous page defines ψ: Ω^*_{X^{(p/S)}/S} → f_*Z^*(Ω^*_{X/S}) → H^*(f_*Ω^*_{X/S}). When this is an isomorphism (after ⊗Λ), it yields C̃: Z^*(f_*Ω^*_{X/S}) → Ω^*_{X^{(p/S)}/S}⊗Λ.

Top of this page: when the map φ exists, its formation is functorial for a commutative square X ← X', S ← S'. Frobenius twists are functorial, so the square induces a commutative prism: X ← X' on top, X^{(p/S)} ← X'^{(p/S')} in the middle, S ← S' at the bottom, with the slanted arrows F_{X/S} and F_{X'/S'}. This is base-change and functoriality compatibility of the Cartier operator.

Section (5), 'Connexions sur les Modules inversibles, et différentielles logarithmiques'.
- Setting: L is an invertible O_X-module with a fixed connection Δ_0 relative to S.
- Parametrisation: every other connection is Δ = Δ_0 + u, with u ∈ Hom(L, L⊗Ω^1_{X/S}) = Γ(Ω^1_{X/S}). So connections on L form a torsor under 1-forms ω.
- Proposition, part 1: if Δ_0 is integrable, Δ_0 + ω is integrable iff dω = 0. This is characteristic-free, and in higher rank it becomes dω + [ω,ω] = 0, as the next page says.
- Proposition, part 2: assume X/X^{(p/S)} has a local p-basis, Δ and Δ_0 are integrable, and Δ_0 has p-curvature zero ('compatible aux puissances p-ièmes'). Then Δ commutes with p-th powers, i.e. Θ_ξ^p = Θ_{ξ^{(p)}} for all local vector fields ξ, iff C̃ω = ω̃⊗1_Λ. Here ω̃ is the Frobenius-twisted form ω^{(p)}.
- Proof (next page): locally choose a p-basis x_i with D_i = ∂/∂x_i, D_i^p = 0. The condition reduces to (Θ^0_{D_i} + c_i)^p = 0, computed by Jacobson's formula.
- Margin idea: define the p-curvature obstruction intrinsically as a section of Ω^1_{X/S}⊗End(E) (Frobenius-twisted), valid in any rank. In rank 1 it equals F^*(ω̃ − C̃ω).
- Special case Δ_0 = d on L = O: d + ω has p-curvature zero iff Cω = ω. These are exactly the forms locally of type dlog, which is Cartier's characterisation of logarithmic differentials. The section serves to connect p-curvature with the Cartier operator.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. Part 2 implicitly needs dω = 0 (guaranteed by the integrability hypothesis on Δ and Δ_0) so that C̃ω is defined.
Equating p-curvature zero with Θ_ξ^p = Θ_{ξ^p} is correct. The notation should strictly distinguish ξ^p (a p-th power of a derivation) from the Frobenius twist; this is harmless here.
The p-basis hypothesis on X/X^{(p/S)} is strong (essentially smooth-like), but it is stated explicitly.

ideas.what: Functoriality and base-change compatibility of the Cartier-type map under squares X'→X over S'→S, via the induced map of Frobenius twists X'^{(p/S')} → X^{(p/S)}
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of relative Frobenius and of the Cartier isomorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier (1957); Katz (1970, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem', §7); Deligne–Illusie (1987)
ideas.where_published: Frobenius twists appear in SGA 5 (exposé XV) and SGA 3; the Cartier functoriality statement itself is unsure

ideas.what: Connections on a line bundle form a torsor under Ω^1; Δ_0 + ω is integrable iff dω = 0 (higher rank: dω + [ω,ω] = 0)
ideas.modern_name: Affine space of connections; flatness / Maurer–Cartan equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cartan); algebraic version in Katz–Oda and Deligne (1970)
ideas.where_published: Crystalline material in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) touches connections; unsure for this exact statement

ideas.what: For a rank-1 connection d+ω (relative to a p-curvature-zero Δ_0), p-curvature vanishes iff Cω = ω^{(p)}; computed via Jacobson's formula on a p-basis
ideas.modern_name: p-curvature of rank-one connections in terms of the Cartier operator: ψ(D) = F^*(ω^{(p)} − Cω)(D)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (1970, Prop. 7.1.2); Cartier (1957) for logarithmic forms Cω = ω

ideas.what: Defining the obstruction to compatibility with p-th powers intrinsically as a section of Ω^1_{X/S}⊗End(E), independent of rank
ideas.modern_name: p-curvature as a Frobenius-linear map / section of F^*Ω^1⊗End(E) (the Higgs field in the Ogus–Vologodsky picture)

ideas.what: Generalised Cartier operator C̃ for X/X^{(p/S)} with a local p-basis, with values in Ω^*⊗Λ where Λ = Im(O_{X^{(p/S)}} → F_*O_X)
ideas.modern_name: Cartier isomorphism for morphisms with p-bases (non-smooth generalisation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier; Katz (1970) in the smooth case; p-basis versions in work of Kimura–Niitsuma and others

missed.claim: This is a Grothendieck-hand treatment of the p-curvature/Cartier relation for rank-1 connections, with the twisted target Λ for X/X^{(p/S)} having only a local p-basis (not necessarily smooth). It also contains the explicit suggestion to define the p-curvature obstruction in End(E)⊗Ω^1 in any rank. This shows Grothendieck engaging with material usually credited to Katz (1970), but the content itself is in the literature.
missed.quote: Supposons que X / X^{p/S} ait loc. une p-bases, et que Δ, Δ0 soient à courbure nulle, avec Δ0 comp. aux puiss. p-ièmes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest: it documents the circulation of ideas between Grothendieck, Cartier and Katz around 1970–72. The p-basis generality is a mild extension, already covered by later work on p-bases.

deep.surprise_reason: The results (connections as a torsor under Ω^1, flatness iff dω = 0, p-curvature zero iff Cω = ω^{(p)}, dlog forms) are standard and published by Katz (1970) and Cartier. The p-basis generality is a modest variation.
transcription_corrections: The first diagram is a square X ← X', S ← S' with vertical arrows. The second is a prism/cube: X ← X' on top, X^{(p/S)} ← X'^{(p/S')} in the middle, S ← S' at the bottom, with slanted arrows X → X^{(p/S)} and X' → X'^{(p/S')} and long arrows X → S and X' → S'. It is not a simple vertical column.
'formes linéaires u : L → L⊗Ω^1' is better read as 'homomorphismes linéaires u'.
The opening is likely 'La formation de φ, dans le cas où il y a existence', referring to the map ψ/C̃ of the previous page.

The heading reads '(5) Connexions sur les Modules inversibles, et différentielles logarithmiques' with the struck-out 'Relations avec les'; the insertion 'muni d'une connexion Δ0 rel/S' attaches to L.
Last line: '(i.e. Θ^p_ξ(x) = Θ_{ξ^p}(x) pour tout champ de vecteurs ξ, sur un ouvert, et x section de L sur celui-ci)' — confirmed.
